findings.message: [fake-timers] `vi.useFakeTimers` is called and no afterEach, afterAll or onTestFinished of the file puts the real timers back: the fake clock leaks into the next test of the worker
findings.fix: Put the real clock back in `afterEach(() => vi.useRealTimers())` (or call installTestKit() from the app's test-setup, which does it after every test).

findings.message: [fake-timers] `vi.useFakeTimers` is called and it puts the real timers back only in a `finally` block, which a test that times out never reaches: the fake clock leaks into the next test of the worker
findings.fix: Put the real clock back in `afterEach(() => vi.useRealTimers())` (or call installTestKit() from the app's test-setup, which does it after every test).

findings.message: [fixed-wait] `flush(DEBOUNCE_MS + 20)` waits a constant plus a guess: too short when the runner is loaded
findings.fix: Wait on the condition: `until(() => ..., { what })` from @decryp7/paddock-ui/testing, `settleUntil` or `vi.waitFor` with an `expect` inside; a constant plus a guess is too short on a loaded runner.

name: lazy-waits

findings.message: [lazy-wait] `vi.waitFor` only imports a module and holds no condition (no `expect`, no `throw`): it waits for nothing
findings.fix: Give the wait a condition that fails until the thing is there (an `expect` or a `throw` on the view), or use `until` from @decryp7/paddock-ui/testing.

findings.message: [lazy-wait] `advanceTimersByTime` is followed directly by an assertion on the view: it runs no promise, so async UI is not there yet
findings.fix: Give the wait a condition that fails until the thing is there (an `expect` or a `throw` on the view), or use `until` from @decryp7/paddock-ui/testing.
